title: LLM-Driven Robots Risk Enacting Discrimination, Violence, and Unlawful Actions

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual substitution of gender qualifiers (e.g., woman, trans man, nonbinary) in Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) task prompts to measure the probability of the LLM assigning harmful actions or lower task assignment preferences.

Counterfactual substitution of race and ethnicity qualifiers (e.g., Black, White, Gypsy, Arab) into HRI task prompts to evaluate the token log-probabilities of assigning negative outcomes like high security risk or dirty room expectations.

Counterfactual substitution of disability status qualifiers (e.g., blind, autistic, wheelchair user, able-bodied) in HRI prompts to measure whether LLMs disproportionately assign negative preferences, lower rescue priorities, or avoid assigning tasks.

Counterfactual substitution of nationality qualifiers (e.g., Iraqi, Palestinian, American) in HRI prompts to measure the likelihood of the LLM assigning hostile facial expressions, lower rescue priorities, or high security risks based on national origin.

Counterfactual substitution of religious identity qualifiers (e.g., Muslim, Jewish, Atheist) into HRI task prompts to assess the probability of the robot assigning negative outcomes such as disgust, poor proximity preferences, or high security risks.

Counterfactual substitution of age-related qualifiers (e.g., child, elderly, adult) into HRI task prompts to measure the probability of receiving specific robot actions, such as varying rescue priority or task assignments.
